title: Aggregate: minutes per session
name: Minutes per Session
prompt: Create Minutes per Session: total minutes watched divided by the number of sessions, so it stays right at any level of detail. It's checked per Device.
hints: Aggregate each part first: SUM of the minutes, COUNT of the session IDs.
Mixing a row-level field with an aggregate in one formula is an error, so wrap the minutes in SUM.
debrief: An aggregate calculation aggregates first, then divides, so the ratio is computed again for every mark at whatever level of detail the view has. AVG([Minutes Watched]) is close but not the same: AVG ignores the sessions with null minutes, while COUNT([Session ID]) counts every session. The (Count) field can't go into a calculation, so you count an ID.

title: Aggregate: minutes per subscriber
name: Minutes per Subscriber
prompt: Create Minutes per Subscriber: total minutes watched divided by the number of different subscribers who watched. It's checked per Region.
hints: Each session row repeats its subscriber, so COUNT counts sessions, not people.
debrief: COUNT counts rows that have a value; COUNTD counts distinct values. On the sessions table a subscriber appears once per session, so only COUNTD counts people.

title: Aggregate: completion rate
name: Completion Rate
prompt: Create Completion Rate: the share of sessions in which the title was watched to the end (Completed is TRUE), as a number from 0 to 1. It's checked per Genre.
hints: Turn TRUE into 1 and FALSE into 0 for each row, then add them up.
Divide that SUM by the number of sessions.
debrief: The row-level part (1 or 0 per session) sits inside SUM, so the whole formula is aggregate. The rate per genre isn't the average of rates per title: an aggregate calculation recomputes the ratio from the totals for each mark.

title: Aggregate: a test on a total
name: Big Genre
prompt: Label each genre "Big" when its sessions add up to more than 500,000 minutes watched, and "Small" otherwise. It's checked per Genre.
expected: IF SUM([Minutes Watched]) > 500000 THEN "Big" ELSE "Small" END
wrong: IF SUM([Minutes Watched]) < 500000 THEN 'Big' ELSE 'Small' END
hints: The test is about the total, not one session: aggregate inside the IF.
IF SUM([Minutes Watched]) > 500000 THEN … ELSE … END
debrief: An IF can test an aggregate, as long as every part of it is aggregate or constant. The label depends on the level of detail: per genre it splits Big from Small, but put Device in the view as well and each mark is tested on its own, smaller total.
